I've been a hightouch customer for nearly a year now, and I have to say the team and product are both great.

Hightouch cofounder explained syncs are declarative: you define a SQL model, and Hightouch figures out how to map it to the destination (e.g. Salesforce Contacts), handling lookups under the hood rather than 1:1 API calls.

Hightouch's hybrid architecture stores no data in Hightouch itself out of the box—it all stays in the customer's own warehouse/S3 bucket—which is why fintech (Plaid, Blend, Betterment) and healthcare (Headway) use them; they have SOC2 Type II certification.
Suggestion from a user: when connecting fields, auto-select a best guess column (e.g. email=>email) to cut configuration time in half, or offer a toggle for this.

Hightouch vs Census comparison from the company: Hightouch offers more developer-focused features (live debugger, alerting, git version control), a business-user UI for visual audience filtering, more transparent pricing, and more/deeper integrations (70+).

User complaint about pushing data into Salesforce via reverse-ETL tools like Hightouch: when Salesforce API returns errors for busy/locked rows, wanted retry with backoff and reporting of permanent failures, noting 'I haven't run across a tool that does this but this was my pain point.'

Blog post titled 'Hightouch Is Just Blindly Copying Rudderstack'; a commenter suggested this explains why Rudderstack changed its license to Elastic, while another called the accusation more like a company feeling threatened by market convergence.
